question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding laterite soil?
option_1: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for crops like cashew nut.
option_2: They are generally rich in humus.
option_3: This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee.
option_4: The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are generally rich in humus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Laterite soil forms in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall through a process called laterization — intense leaching removes silica and soluble minerals, leaving behind oxides of iron and aluminium, which give the soil its characteristic red colour. (लेटराइट मिट्टी — उच्च तापमान और भारी वर्षा में निर्मित)

 

• Because of this intense leaching, laterite soils are generally poor in nitrogen, phosphate, calcium and humus — the statement calling them "rich in humus" is factually incorrect.

 

• Red laterite soils found in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are well suited to crops such as cashew nut.

 

• Laterite soil is also well suited for plantation crops like tea, coffee, rubber and cinchona, especially in the hilly tracts of Karnataka, Kerala, Assam and Tamil Nadu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Laterite soils cover parts of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and the north-eastern states.

 

• The word "laterite" comes from the Latin "later", meaning brick — the soil hardens into brick-like blocks on exposure to air and is used as a building material.

 

NOTE

 

• Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu... (Option 1): A correct statement — cashew nut is widely cultivated on laterite soils in these states.

 

• This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee. (Option 3): A correct statement — laterite soils support plantation agriculture like tea and coffee.

 

• The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall. (Option 4): A correct statement — laterization requires high temperature with alternating wet and dry seasons.

question: In which of the following countries was the 2022 Cricket Asia Cup held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Arab Emirates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Asia Cup (T20 format) was originally slated to be hosted by Sri Lanka, but due to the severe economic and political crisis in the country at the time, the tournament venue was shifted to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). (एशिया कप 2022 — संयुक्त अरब अमीरात में आयोजित)

 

• It was held from 27 August to 11 September 2022 across Dubai and Sharjah, played in the T20 format as a lead-up to the T20 World Cup 2022.

 

• Sri Lanka won the 2022 Asia Cup title, defeating Pakistan in the final, even though the tournament was physically hosted in the UAE.

 

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) among the leading cricket-playing nations of Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 Asia Cup (ODI format) was hosted jointly by Pakistan and Sri Lanka under a "hybrid model", with India's matches played in Sri Lanka.

 

• India has won the Asia Cup the most number of times among all participating nations.

 

NOTE

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 2): Sri Lanka was the original designated host and went on to win the 2022 title, but the tournament itself was relocated to the UAE.

 

• India (Option 3): India did not host the 2022 edition of the Asia Cup.

 

• China (Option 4): China is not a competitive cricket-playing nation and has never hosted the Asia Cup.

question: Which team won the Vijay Hazare trophy 2021 – 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Himachal Pradesh won its maiden Vijay Hazare Trophy title in the 2021–22 season, defeating Tamil Nadu in the final held at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium, Jaipur, on 26 December 2021. (विजय हजारे ट्रॉफी – हिमाचल प्रदेश की पहली खिताबी जीत)

 

• All-rounder Rishi Dhawan was the standout performer for Himachal Pradesh, contributing significantly with both bat and ball through the tournament.

 

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is India's premier domestic List A (50-over) cricket tournament, organised by the BCCI and named after former Indian cricketer Vijay Hazare.

 

• This victory marked Himachal Pradesh's first-ever domestic 50-over title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy has been contested annually since the 2002–03 season and serves as an important selection pathway for the Indian ODI team.

 

• Mumbai and Tamil Nadu are among the historically most successful teams in the tournament.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): A strong domestic side, but did not win the 2021–22 edition.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Reached the final of the 2021–22 edition but lost to Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Mumbai (Option 4): Historically the most successful team in the Vijay Hazare Trophy, but did not win this particular edition.

question: The total pressure of a mixture of ideal gases is the sum of partial pressures. This is ______ law of partial pressures.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dalton's.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures, given by John Dalton, states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting (ideal) gases equals the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas in the mixture. (डाल्टन का आंशिक दाब का नियम)

 

• Mathematically, P(total) = P1 + P2 + P3 + ..., where each Pn is the pressure a gas would exert if it alone occupied the entire container at the same temperature.

 

• The law applies to gases that do not chemically react with one another and assumes ideal gas behaviour.

 

• It has practical applications in fields like respiratory physiology, scuba diving and industrial gas mixing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• John Dalton is also known for proposing the modern Atomic Theory in the early 19th century.

 

• Other classic gas laws include Boyle's Law (P ∝ 1/V at constant temperature) and Charles' Law (V ∝ T at constant pressure).

 

NOTE

 

• Boyles' (Option 2): Boyle's Law relates the pressure and volume of a gas at constant temperature, not partial pressures of a mixture.

 

• Charles' (Option 3): Charles' Law relates the volume and temperature of a gas at constant pressure.

 

• Avogadro's (Option 4): Avogadro's Law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

question: Which among the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the right to equality of opportunity in the matters of public employment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 16 of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State. (अनुच्छेद 16 — लोक नियोजन के विषय में अवसर की समानता)

 

• It falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights), specifically the Right to Equality.

 

• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence with regard to public employment, while allowing the State to make special provisions for reservation of backward classes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth more generally (not restricted to employment).

 

• Articles 17 and 18 deal with the abolition of untouchability and the abolition of titles, respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• 17 (Option 1): Article 17 abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.

 

• 18 (Option 2): Article 18 abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.

 

• 15 (Option 3): Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth in general, not specifically in public employment.

question: Who among the following is the Union Minister of Law and Justice of India as of October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiren Rijiju.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kiren Rijiju served as the Union Minister of Law and Justice from July 2021, and continued to hold this portfolio as of October 2022. (किरेन रिजिजू — विधि और न्याय मंत्री)

 

• He is a BJP leader and Member of Parliament from Arunachal West, Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• He had earlier served as Minister of State for Home Affairs and as Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kiren Rijiju was later moved to the Ministry of Earth Sciences in a cabinet reshuffle in May 2023, with Arjun Ram Meghwal taking over the Law and Justice portfolio.

 

• He is a former national-level taekwondo player from Arunachal Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Raj Kumar Singh (Option 2): He held the portfolio of Union Minister of Power and New & Renewable Energy at the time.

 

• Pralhad Joshi (Option 3): He served as Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines.

 

• Bhupender Yadav (Option 4): He served as Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and Labour and Employment.

question: Which among the following is Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanwar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanwar Lake (also called Kabartal Wetland), located in Begusarai district, Bihar, is recognised as Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake. (कंवर झील / काबरताल आर्द्रभूमि — एशिया की सबसे बड़ी मीठे पानी की गोखुर झील)

 

• An oxbow lake is a crescent-shaped water body formed when a meandering river channel gets cut off from the main river; Kanwar Lake formed from an old channel of the Gandak-Baya-Ganga river system.

 

• It was designated a Ramsar Site (wetland of international importance) in 2020 and also functions as an important bird sanctuary hosting many migratory species.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihar has three Ramsar sites: Kanwar (Kabartal) Lake, Nagi Bird Sanctuary and Nakti Bird Sanctuary.

 

• Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake overall, but it is not an oxbow lake.

 

NOTE

 

• Wular (Option 1): Wular Lake, Jammu & Kashmir, is India's largest freshwater lake, formed by tectonic activity, not an oxbow lake.

 

• Bhojtal (Option 3): Bhojtal (Upper Lake), in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, is a man-made lake built by King Bhoja.

 

• Nakki (Option 4): Nakki Lake is a natural lake located in Mount Abu, Rajasthan.

question: Flute instruments comes under which type of instrument category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sushira Vadya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the traditional Indian classification of musical instruments, wind instruments like the flute (bansuri), shehnai and nadaswaram fall under the Sushira Vadya category. (सुषिर वाद्य — फूंक कर बजाए जाने वाले वाद्य)

 

• Indian instruments are broadly classified into four categories: Tata (chordophones/string), Avanaddha (membranophones/percussion covered with skin), Ghana (idiophones/solid, self-sonorous instruments) and Sushira (aerophones/wind instruments).

 

• "Sushira" literally means "hollow" — sound is produced by blowing air through a hollow tube or pipe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of Sushira Vadya include the shehnai, nadaswaram and harmonium.

 

• The tabla and mridangam are examples of Avanaddha Vadya, while the sitar and veena are examples of Tata Vadya.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghana Vadya (Option 1): Solid, self-sonorous instruments like manjira (cymbals) and jaltarang fall in this category.

 

• Avanaddha Vadya (Option 3): Percussion instruments covered with a membrane/skin, such as the tabla and mridangam, belong to this category.

 

• Tata Vadya (Option 4): Stringed instruments like the sitar, veena and violin belong to this category.

question: Bhagwant Singh Mann is an Indian politician and current Chief Minister of Punjab. He was formerly a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is comedian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhagwant Singh Mann is an Indian politician of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) who became the Chief Minister of Punjab in March 2022. (भगवंत मान — पंजाब के मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• Before entering politics, he was a popular comedian in the Punjabi entertainment industry, known for his comic performances and stage shows.

 

• He first entered active politics with the Manpreet Badal-led Peoples Party of Punjab before later joining AAP.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhagwant Mann led AAP to a landslide victory in the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, winning 92 out of 117 seats.

 

• He had earlier served as a Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from Sangrur before becoming Chief Minister.

 

NOTE

 

• cricketer (Option 2): Bhagwant Mann is not a former cricketer.

 

• writer (Option 3): He is not primarily known as a writer.

 

• singer (Option 4): He is not a former singer; his public fame came from stand-up comedy and political satire.

question: The important system components like the central processing unit (CPU) and random access memory (RAM) modules are connected directly to the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mother Board.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Motherboard is the primary circuit board of a computer that houses and directly connects critical components such as the Central Processing Unit (CPU) and Random Access Memory (RAM) modules. (मदरबोर्ड — कंप्यूटर का मुख्य परिपथ बोर्ड)

 

• It provides the electrical connections, sockets and slots through which the CPU, RAM, expansion cards and other components communicate with each other.

 

• It also houses the BIOS/UEFI chip, along with ports for storage devices, the power supply and peripherals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The motherboard's chipset manages the flow of data between the CPU, RAM, storage and peripheral devices.

 

• Common motherboard form factors include ATX, Micro-ATX and Mini-ITX.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnetic Tape (Option 1): A sequential secondary storage medium, mainly used for data backup and archiving.

 

• Optical Disk (Option 3): A storage medium (such as CDs and DVDs) that uses laser technology to read and write data.

 

• Flash Memory (Option 4): A non-volatile secondary storage medium (e.g., USB drives, SSDs) used for storing data, not for direct component interconnection.

question: When was the Champaran Agrarian Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1918.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 was passed following the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Mahatma Gandhi's first major civil disobedience movement in India, launched in Bihar's Champaran district against the forced cultivation of indigo under the Tinkathia system. (चंपारण कृषि अधिनियम, 1918)

 

• The Act abolished the Tinkathia system and provided relief to the indigo cultivators (ryots) who were being exploited by British planters.

 

• The success of the Champaran movement, achieved through Gandhi's method of Satyagraha, established him as a major leader of the Indian freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's associates in the Champaran Satyagraha included Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha and J. B. Kripalani.

 

• The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was followed by the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918), Gandhi's other early movements in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1920 (Option 1): 1920 is associated with the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhi, not the Champaran Agrarian Act.

 

• 1922 (Option 2): 1922 is associated with the Chauri Chaura incident and the subsequent withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• 1924 (Option 4): 1924 does not correspond to the passage of the Champaran Agrarian Act.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the direct taxes?
I. Levied on taxable income earned by individuals and corporate entities.
II. Gift tax is a type of direct tax.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Direct taxes are levied directly on the taxable income or wealth of individuals and corporate entities, and their burden cannot be shifted to another person — making Statement I correct. (प्रत्यक्ष कर — आय पर सीधे लगाया गया कर)

 

• Gift tax is levied on the recipient of a gift (in cash, property or other assets) above a specified threshold, and is administered as part of the Income Tax Act — it is classified as a direct tax, making Statement II correct as well.

 

• Other examples of direct taxes in India include Income Tax, Corporate Tax, Wealth Tax (abolished in 2015) and Capital Gains Tax.

 

• In contrast, indirect taxes (like GST, customs duty and excise duty) are levied on goods and services, and their burden can be passed on to the final consumer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Direct taxes in India are administered and collected under the oversight of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).

 

• Gift tax was reintroduced as part of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (via the Finance Act, 2004), after the original Gift Tax Act, 1958 was abolished in 1998.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete — Statement II (gift tax being a direct tax) is also correct.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incomplete — Statement I (direct tax levied on taxable income) is also correct.

question: Before writing codes in a high level language, a ______ of a program helps in representing the basic functionality of the intended program.
solution_text:
The correct answer is pseudocode.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A pseudocode is an informal, plain-language description of the steps of an algorithm or program, written before actual coding begins, to represent the basic logic and functionality of the intended program. (स्यूडोकोड — कार्यक्रम के तर्क का सरल विवरण)

 

• It uses structured, English-like statements (such as IF, WHILE, FOR) without following the strict syntax rules of any particular high-level programming language.

 

• Pseudocode helps programmers plan, communicate and verify the logic of a program before writing actual code, making design review and debugging easier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pseudocode is often used alongside flowcharts, another tool used to visually represent an algorithm's logic before implementation.

 

• Since pseudocode is not tied to any specific programming language's syntax, it can be easily translated into any high-level language such as C, Java or Python.

 

NOTE

 

• original code (Option 1): Not a standard term for pre-coding program design; "source code"/"original code" typically refers to actual written code.

 

• small code (Option 2): Not a recognised technical term for describing pre-coding program logic.

 

• naïve code (Option 3): Not a standard programming term used in this context.

question:
Which of the following pair of "player – sports" is correct?
I. Bajrang Punia – Boxing
II. Yash Dhull – Cricket
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bajrang Punia is a celebrated Indian wrestler, not a boxer — he is an Olympic bronze medallist (Tokyo 2020) and a multiple-time World Championship medallist in freestyle wrestling, so Statement I is incorrect. (बजरंग पुनिया — भारतीय पहलवान)

 

• Yash Dhull is an Indian cricketer who captained the Indian Under-19 cricket team to victory in the 2022 U-19 Cricket World Cup, making Statement II a correct pairing.

 

• Hence, only Statement II presents a correct player–sport pairing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yash Dhull went on to earn a call-up to the Delhi Ranji Trophy squad and India A teams as a top-order batter.

 

• Bajrang Punia competes in the 65 kg freestyle wrestling category and trained at the Chhatrasal Stadium akhara in Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, since Bajrang Punia is a wrestler, not a boxer.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement I wrongly pairs Bajrang Punia with boxing.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement II (Yash Dhull – Cricket) is a correct pairing.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding sound?
option_2: In human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produces sound.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sound can travel through vacuum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel, since it propagates through the vibration of particles of that medium — it cannot travel through a vacuum, as there are no particles to carry the vibrations. (ध्वनि तरंग — निर्वात में संचरित नहीं हो सकती)

 

• This makes the statement "Sound can travel through vacuum" factually incorrect, which is why it is the correct answer to this "NOT correct" question.

 

• In human beings, sound is produced by the vibration of the vocal cords, located in the larynx (voice box).

 

• The frequency of sound is measured in hertz (Hz), and unpleasant or disturbing sounds are termed noise, as opposed to pleasant, rhythmic sounds called music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sound travels fastest through solids, slower through liquids, and slowest through gases, due to differences in particle density and elasticity of the medium.

 

• The speed of sound in dry air at 0°C is approximately 331 m/s.

 

NOTE

 

• In human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produces sound. (Option 2): A correct statement — sound in humans is produced by the vibration of the vocal cords.

 

• Unpleasant sounds are called noise. (Option 3): A correct statement — noise refers to unpleasant, non-rhythmic sound.

 

• Frequency is expressed in hertz. (Option 4): A correct statement — frequency, the number of vibrations per second, is measured in hertz (Hz).

question: The reproduction in yeast happens by the process of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Budding.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yeast, a unicellular fungus, reproduces asexually mainly through the process of budding, in which a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent cell, grows, and eventually separates to form a new individual. (यीस्ट में जनन — मुकुलन/बडिंग द्वारा)

 

• During budding, the nucleus of the parent cell divides, and one of the daughter nuclei migrates into the developing bud, which then detaches once it matures.

 

• Under favourable conditions (adequate nutrients, moisture and temperature), yeast can reproduce rapidly through repeated budding, sometimes forming chains of cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under unfavourable conditions, some yeast species can also reproduce through spore formation (ascospores).

 

• Yeast, particularly *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, is widely used in baking and brewing owing to its fermentation ability.

 

NOTE

 

• Fragmentation (Option 2): A method of asexual reproduction seen in organisms like *Spirogyra*, not the primary method in yeast.

 

• Spore formation (Option 3): Occurs in yeast only under unfavourable/stress conditions, and is not its typical mode of reproduction.

 

• Fertilisation (Option 4): A form of sexual reproduction involving the fusion of gametes, not the usual mode of reproduction in yeast.

question: PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) is associated with which organization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ISRO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) is a platform developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) that uses the final, spent stage of the PSLV rocket as a stabilised orbital platform for conducting in-orbit scientific experiments. (पीएसएलवी ऑर्बिटल एक्सपेरिमेंटल मॉड्यूल — इसरो)

 

• It was first successfully demonstrated during the PSLV-C53 mission in June 2022, where the fourth stage (PS4) of the rocket, instead of becoming space debris, was converted into a functioning experimental platform.

 

• POEM allows small experimental payloads — including from startups and academic institutions — to be tested in a microgravity space environment without requiring a dedicated satellite launch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subsequent missions (POEM-2, POEM-3, POEM-4) have continued this concept on later PSLV flights, including PSLV-C58 and the SpaDeX mission.

 

• POEM forms part of ISRO's broader efforts toward sustainable, debris-minimising space operations.

 

NOTE

 

• DRDO (Option 1): The Defence Research and Development Organisation works on India's defence research and technology, not POEM.

 

• HAL (Option 2): Hindustan Aeronautics Limited manufactures aircraft and aerospace equipment, primarily for defence.

 

• BHEL (Option 3): Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited is a public sector engineering and manufacturing company in the power and heavy-equipment sector.

question: Who was professor Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis?
option_1: Economist who won a Nobel Prize
option_2: An artist who painted the painting of Bharat Mata
option_4: A doctor who invented a new surgical method
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Scientist and Statistician.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Professor Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was an eminent Indian scientist and statistician, best known for introducing the statistical measure called the "Mahalanobis Distance". (प्रशांत चंद्र महालनोबिस — भारतीय वैज्ञानिक एवं सांख्यिकीविद)

 

• He founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Kolkata in 1931 and played a key role in formulating India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61), which emphasised rapid industrialisation — this planning approach is known as the Mahalanobis Model.

 

• He is regarded as the father of modern statistics in India, and National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June every year, his birth anniversary, in his honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahalanobis was also a member of the first Planning Commission of India and served on several international statistical bodies, including the United Nations Sub-Commission on Statistical Sampling.

 

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1968 for his contributions to science and statistics.

 

NOTE

 

• Economist who won a Nobel Prize (Option 1): Does not describe Mahalanobis; he was a statistician, not a Nobel laureate economist.

 

• An artist who painted the painting of Bharat Mata (Option 2): This refers to Abanindranath Tagore, who painted the famous "Bharat Mata" (1905).

 

• A doctor who invented a new surgical method (Option 4): Does not correspond to Mahalanobis, who was a statistician, not a medical doctor.

question: The Dronacharya Award was first handed out in 1985, and the first Dronacharya Award winner was _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dronacharya Award, India's highest recognition for sports coaches, was instituted in 1985 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. (द्रोणाचार्य पुरस्कार — भारत का सर्वोच्च खेल प्रशिक्षक सम्मान)

 

• Among the first batch of recipients in 1985 was Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat, a noted wrestling coach, widely recognised as the first-ever recipient of the award.

 

• The award is named after Dronacharya, the legendary guru of the Kauravas and Pandavas in the Mahabharata, symbolising excellence in coaching.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dronacharya Award carries a statuette, a citation, ceremonial dress and a cash prize, presented by the President of India.

 

• Notable later recipients span disciplines such as athletics, badminton, boxing and hockey.

 

NOTE

 

• Hansa Sharma (Option 1): Not associated with being the first Dronacharya Award recipient.

 

• Karan Singh (Option 2): Not the first recipient of the Dronacharya Award.

 

• Hawa Singh (Option 4): Hawa Singh is known as a boxer and Arjuna Award recipient, not the first Dronacharya awardee.

question: Surat is also known as ______ of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diamond city.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Surat, located in Gujarat, is known as the "Diamond City of India" because it is the world's leading centre for diamond cutting and polishing, processing a large majority of the world's rough diamonds. (सूरत — भारत का हीरा नगर)

 

• The city is also a major hub for the textile and zari (embroidery) industry, which has earned it additional nicknames such as "Silk City" and "Textile City" of India.

 

• Surat is situated on the banks of the Tapti (Tapi) River and was historically an important trading port during the Mughal era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surat has consistently ranked among the cleanest and fastest-growing cities in India in various government surveys.

 

• The Surat Diamond Bourse, inaugurated in 2023, is one of the world's largest office buildings, built to boost the city's diamond trade.

 

NOTE

 

• Blue city (Option 2): This nickname refers to Jodhpur, Rajasthan, known for its blue-painted houses.

 

• Pink City (Option 3): This nickname refers to Jaipur, Rajasthan, known for its pink-coloured buildings.

 

• City of Lakes (Option 4): This nickname is commonly associated with Udaipur, Rajasthan, known for its numerous lakes.

question: The northern plains of India are formed up of which soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alluvial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Northern Plains of India, formed by the rivers Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra along with their tributaries, are made up of alluvial soil — fine sediments of sand, silt and clay deposited by these rivers over millions of years. (उत्तरी मैदान — जलोढ़ मिट्टी से निर्मित)

 

• Alluvial soil is highly fertile and rich in potash and lime, but generally low in nitrogen and organic matter, making it ideal for intensive agriculture.

 

• The Northern Plains are broadly classified into Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar (older alluvium) and Khadar (newer alluvium), based on the nature and age of the alluvial deposits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Northern Plains are among the most densely populated and agriculturally productive regions in the world, supporting crops like wheat, rice and sugarcane.

 

• Alluvial soil covers roughly 40% of India's total land area, mainly across the Indo-Gangetic plains and river deltas.

 

NOTE

 

• Peaty (Option 2): Peaty/marshy soils, rich in organic and humus content, are found in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity, such as parts of Kerala, Odisha and West Bengal.

 

• Black (Option 3): Black (regur) soil, ideal for cotton cultivation, is found mainly in the Deccan Plateau region (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat).

 

• Laterite (Option 4): Laterite soil forms in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall, found mainly in the plateau regions of peninsular India.

question: Start Up India Scheme which aims at developing an ecosystem that promotes and nurtures entrepreneurship across the country was launched in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Start-up India Scheme was launched by the Government of India on 16 January 2016, aimed at building a strong ecosystem to promote and nurture innovation and entrepreneurship across the country. (स्टार्टअप इंडिया योजना — 2016 में शुरू)

 

• It offers benefits such as tax exemptions, easier compliance, funding support through the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), and self-certification under labour and environment laws.

 

• The scheme is administered by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi first announced the Start-up India initiative in his Independence Day speech on 15 August 2015.

 

• "National Start-up Day" is observed on 16 January every year to commemorate the launch of the scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• 2020 (Option 2): Not the year the Start-up India Scheme was launched.

 

• 2012 (Option 3): Not the year the Start-up India Scheme was launched.

 

• 2018 (Option 4): Not the year the Start-up India Scheme was launched.

question: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1940.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1940, at its Lahore session, the All-India Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, passed the Lahore Resolution (later also referred to as the "Pakistan Resolution"), demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of British India. (लाहौर प्रस्ताव, 1940 – मुस्लिम लीग)

 

• This resolution is widely regarded as the formal articulation of the Two-Nation Theory and laid the ideological foundation for the eventual creation of Pakistan in 1947.

 

• The resolution was moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq, the Chief Minister of Bengal, at the Lahore session held on 22–24 March 1940.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "Pakistan" for the demanded state gained wider currency after this resolution, though the word "Pakistan" itself did not appear in the original text.

 

• The Muslim League later reiterated its demand for Pakistan through the "Direct Action Day" call in August 1946.

 

NOTE

 

• 1942 (Option 2): 1942 is associated with the Quit India Movement and the Cripps Mission, not the Lahore Resolution.

 

• 1946 (Option 3): 1946 is associated with the Cabinet Mission Plan and the Direct Action Day called by the Muslim League.

 

• 1935 (Option 4): 1935 is associated with the Government of India Act, 1935, not the Lahore Resolution.

question: Thangka painting style depicts ______ deity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buddhist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thangka is a traditional Tibetan Buddhist painting style, typically made on cotton or silk, depicting Buddhist deities, mandalas, or scenes from the life of the Buddha. (थंगका चित्रकला — बौद्ध देवी-देवताओं का चित्रण)

 

• Thangkas serve as important teaching tools illustrating the life of the Buddha and various lamas and bodhisattvas, and are also used in religious rituals and meditation practice.

 

• This art form is prevalent in regions with strong Tibetan Buddhist influence, such as Ladakh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh in India, as well as Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan and Mongolia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thangkas are often mounted on colourful silk brocade and can be rolled up when not on display, making them portable for monks and travellers.

 

• Other notable Indian Buddhist art forms/sites include the murals of Ajanta and Alchi, and the stupas of Sanchi.

 

NOTE

 

• Islamic (Option 1): Islamic art traditionally avoids figural depiction of deities and emphasises calligraphy and geometric patterns instead.

 

• Jewish (Option 3): Judaism similarly does not have a deity-depicting painting tradition; the Thangka style is unrelated to Jewish art.

 

• Hindu (Option 4): Hindu deities are more commonly depicted through styles such as Pattachitra, Tanjore and Madhubani paintings, not Thangka.

question: In India, Who was appointed the new Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anil Chauhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• General Anil Chauhan (Retd.) was appointed as India's second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on 28 September 2022. (जनरल अनिल चौहान — भारत के द्वितीय रक्षा प्रमुख)

 

• He succeeded General Bipin Rawat, India's first CDS, who died in a helicopter crash in December 2021; the post had remained vacant for over nine months before General Chauhan's appointment.

 

• General Chauhan had earlier served as the Eastern Army Commander and later as Military Adviser to the National Security Council Secretariat before his appointment as CDS.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The post of CDS was created in December 2019 to serve as the single-point military adviser to the government and to head the Department of Military Affairs.

 

• As CDS, General Chauhan also functions as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• Yogendra Dimri (Option 1): Not appointed as CDS; not associated with this position.

 

• Rana Pratap Kalita (Option 2): He served as the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Eastern Command of the Indian Army, not as CDS.

 

• Manoj Mukund Naravane (Option 4): He served as the Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) until April 2022, not as CDS.
